scope: Initial Foundation seed questions in Discussion 38
takeaway: The initial review agenda asks whether Draft v1 is legally administrable, technically measurable, economically proportionate, secure across heterogeneous hardware, and practically accessible beyond people who already own capable devices.

themes.title: Capability measures must fit the architecture
themes.summary: The spatial and world-model classification question asks whether a general-purpose training-compute threshold is a defensible proxy or whether architecture-specific, multi-factor evidence is needed.

themes.title: State and federal enactment paths need separate analysis
themes.summary: The jurisdiction question asks whether state administration needs clearer territorial nexus, safe-harbor, reciprocity, or preemption language for interstate AI services.

themes.title: Public support reciprocity needs an evidence-based clock
themes.summary: The economic question asks whether 18 months is proportionate to AI development cycles and how waivers, security constraints, third-party rights, and open-research alternatives should work.

themes.title: Node assurance must remain vendor-neutral and privacy-preserving
themes.summary: The security question asks for a minimum tamper-evident outcome across old and new hardware without turning attestation into surveillance, lock-in, or a barrier to recovery and reuse.

themes.title: Legal access is not the same as practical access
themes.summary: The accessibility question asks whether Draft v2 should address equipment, connectivity, support, disability access, language, and digital literacy without requiring centralized monitoring or compelled cloud use.

open_questions: What evidence should replace or supplement parameter count and general-purpose FLOP thresholds for world models?
What jurisdictional limits make a state version enforceable without regulating wholly out-of-state conduct?
What reciprocity trigger and period preserve public benefit without defeating legitimate commercialization or security obligations?
What minimum node evidence is auditable, owner-controlled, recoverable, and usable across heterogeneous hardware?
What practical-access mechanisms close disability and digital-divide gaps without creating surveillance or an unfunded mandate?
